searches.reason: Develop practical probes of whether GRU4Rec responds to current intent: compare original histories with recent-item removal, older-prefix removal, and order perturbations, measuring target-rank and top-10 changes. Include padding-invariance checks and final-nonpadding readout verification. Treat perturbations as sensitivity evidence, not proof of causal user intent.

searches.reason: Translate qualitative feedback into measurable failure modes using only histories, timestamps, titles, descriptions, and explicitly collected feedback. Seek methods that distinguish recent-interest alignment, possible redundancy, and unclear item identity while retaining an unknown state for unsupported compatibility, ownership, mood, or purchase-intent claims. Validate text-based proxies against the twenty training-user feedback cases without inferring hidden traits.

searches.reason: Establish whether diagnostic signals predict actionable failures rather than score scale or negative-sampling artifacts. Seek paired rank-based measurements, popularity and history-length stratification, uncertainty estimates, and calibration against controlled interventions within one GRU4Rec model per category. Keep the pinned validation evaluator unchanged and use training-only prefix targets for additional ranking probes.
